I decided to get out of comfort zone and cook things I'm not used to. This week's experiment was _SAVILLVM_, an ancient version of cheesecake from Rome (recipe < from this very interesting channel about history of food!) My result was a darker cake than the one in the post (I believe the author used Barley, I used whole wheat). It's denser than modern cheesecakes and just mildly reminiscent of cheese (I also used ricotta). I liked it, it's a very simple recipe with simple ingredients and processes.
What was the consistency like? Was it very sweet?
it was denser that a cheesecake, kind of like a bread (but moisty). Not very sweet - I used the amount of honey in the recipe and I still drizzled a bit more when serving because I like it sweeter.
